subagent_reports.architecture_assessment: Design makes correctness structural at the Temporal reducer boundary (applyEntryTerminalSummaryToState), the canonical fix for an invariant that must hold across many callers. Source evidence confirms the split the design describes: reducer writes only terminal_summary (epic-state.ts:687-690) while the direct-link tool path additionally sets membership_status=terminal (epic.ts:391-402), and summary-only callers (archive-gate.ts:516-520, plus epic.ts:2997/3193) leave membership stale. Spec rq-epicTerminalChildProjection01 (spec.json:1142-1178) requires the two fields to move together; reducer enforcement means every present and future caller inherits the invariant, aligning with P33 (structural before heuristic) and repo convention that per-change/entry workflow state is source of truth. The renderer already keys on membership_status (epic.ts:112-141), so no display-only override is introduced, satisfying the agreement avoidance against masking drift. Explicit failure/warning paths (KD2) already exist at the tool/archive layer and are preserved. Spec-scope nuance: the prose invariant is written against adv_epic_link_change specifically; the design correctly generalizes it as a reducer-level superset rather than narrowing or contradicting it — no spec law is violated. One implementation note: the current reducer records idempotency AFTER the write (epic-state.ts:693), so adding membership_status=terminal in the same mutation block is replay-safe (DDC4).

validation.notes: Design is spec-law compliant and source-evidence-backed. rq-epicTerminalChildProjection01 (spec.json:1142-1178) requires terminal_summary + membership_status=terminal together; reducer-level enforcement is a compliant superset that satisfies the link-scoped requirement and closes the seam for summary-only callers (archive-gate.ts:516-520). No contradiction with one-Epic-per-change, optional membership, advisory order, or Temporal signal/query architecture. KD2 explicit-failure preservation matches existing archive-gate.ts:526 warning path. KD3 redundant setEntryMembershipStatus call at epic.ts:397 is genuinely redundant post-normalization and correctly gated behind RED/GREEN regression proof. Implementation note (not a blocker): place the membership_status=terminal write in the same mutation block before the idempotency record (epic-state.ts:687-693) so idempotent replay (DDC4) stays safe.

tradeoffs: Reducer-level normalization changes behavior for ALL entryTerminalSummary callers, not just the buggy ones — intended and desirable, but widens blast radius so requires reducer/workflow coverage plus at least one previously summary-only caller-path assertion (design provides both).

Leaving the redundant setEntryMembershipStatus call (epic.ts:397) minimizes churn but keeps a now-dead write; removing it is cleaner but needs regression proof of response shape and error behavior. Design correctly defers this to test-gated cleanup rather than forcing it.

documents.proposal:
# Fix epic terminal projection

## Why

When an Epic-linked change is archived or terminal state is synchronized, ADV records a `terminal_summary` on the Epic entry but may leave `membership_status` as `projection_pending`, `projection_stale`, or `target_unreachable`. That can make terminal Epic history appear to need repair even though terminal projection exists.

Desired outcome: terminal child projection should be internally consistent and spec-aligned: Epic entries with terminal summaries should also reflect terminal membership status, with tests guarding the archive/sync path.

## What Changes

This change proposes a focused correction to Epic terminal child projection:

- Align the terminal summary projection path with the Epic membership-status contract.
- Ensure archived/closed child projection cannot leave terminal Epic history in a repair-needed or projection-missing-looking state.
- Preserve typed error behavior if projection fails; failures should remain visible instead of being hidden by display heuristics.
- Add focused tests around the real reducer/tool path so mocks do not mask the mismatch.
- Preserve the current Epic architecture: typed Epic containers, shell/change entries, compact child `epic_membership`, advisory ordering, and explicit cross-project routing.

## User Outcomes

- ADV users see terminal Epic history as complete and consistent, not as needing repair after archive/sync.
- Maintainers can trust Epic repair/status output when deciding whether a terminal child entry still needs action.
- Projection failures remain explicit and actionable rather than being hidden by formatting.
- Future Epic work has a structural test guard for terminal projection consistency.

## Affected Code

Likely areas for discovery validation:

- `plugin/src/temporal/epic-state.ts` — `applyEntryTerminalSummaryToState` currently records `terminal_summary`.
- `plugin/src/tools/epic.ts` — link/repair paths that project terminal state and render member status.
- `plugin/src/tools/change/archive-gate.ts` — archive-time Epic terminal-summary fan-out.
- `plugin/src/types/epics.ts` — `EpicMembershipStatusSchema` includes `terminal`.
- Tests near `plugin/src/temporal/epic-state.test.ts`, `plugin/src/tools/epic.test.ts`, and `plugin/src/tools/change.archive-phase9.test.ts`.

## Related Repositories

- Current repo only: `/home/jon/dev/advance`.
- No product-linked cross-repo scope identified.

## Constraints

- Specs are law: preserve `advance-epics` requirements, especially `rq-epicTerminalChildProjection01` and `rq-epicArchiveSync01`.
- Preserve current Epic architecture; do not redesign Epic membership, entry kinds, ordering, or cross-project ownership.
- Preserve one-Epic-per-change v1 invariant.
- Preserve advisory Epic ordering and optional Epic membership.
- Preserve typed Temporal signal/query architecture; do not introduce update-based mutation surfaces.
- Preserve explicit failure behavior for projection/update failures; do not convert real projection failures into silent success or display-only fixes.
- Keep change focused; do not fold in broad adapter cleanup or dashboard/indexing work.

## Impact

Expected impact is correctness and operator trust in Epic terminal history/status. User-visible change should be limited to terminal Epic entries no longer surfacing misleading projection/repair status after terminal projection. Real projection failures should remain visible through existing typed error/reporting paths.

## Context

Evidence gathered during idea shaping and proposal:

- `advance-epics` requires terminal child projection to set terminal summary and terminal membership status, and later Epic show must not flag the repaired terminal entry.
- `plugin/src/temporal/epic-state.ts:687-690` records `terminal_summary` but does not set `membership_status`.
- `plugin/src/tools/epic.ts` renders `membership_status: "terminal"` as OK, showing the status value is expected by presentation code.
- Existing tests include mocks with `membership_status: "terminal"`, which may mask whether the real reducer/tool path writes it.
- Active adjacent change `optimizeAdapterSurfaces` targets broader adapter coupling and should remain separate from this focused spec-alignment fix.

## Scope

### In Scope

- Correcting terminal child projection consistency for Epic entries.
- Tests proving terminal summary projection also produces terminal membership status where required.
- Archive/sync/link-path verification where discovery confirms the mismatch exists.
- Error-path verification where the chosen fix could alter projection failure behavior.
- Minimal documentation or wisdom updates if discovery/design identifies a durable convention.

### Out of Scope

- Full Epic architecture redesign.
- Cross-project shell promotion.
- New `AdvEpicScope` or dashboard search attributes.
- Broad adapter-surface refactoring.
- New Epic planning primitives, mandatory Epic membership, or Jira-like workflow concepts.
- Changes to Epic ordering, promotion, retirement, or product-scope semantics unless directly required by terminal projection consistency.

### Must Not

- Must not weaken `rq-epicTerminalChildProjection01` or `rq-epicArchiveSync01`.
- Must not treat terminal entries as repaired by display heuristics alone if underlying typed state remains inconsistent.
- Must not bypass typed Epic tools, reducers, or Temporal signal/query contracts.
- Must not add direct ADV state-file reads.
- Must not make Epic membership mandatory or multi-valued.
- Must not hide real projection/update failures or convert them into silent success.
- Must not merge this focused fix into unrelated performance/adapter refactor work.

## Discovery Findings

### Discovery Checklist

### Skills Considered

- `adv-audit`: loaded. Match: spec/implementation drift against `advance-epics` MUST requirements.
- `adv-arch-detection`: loaded. Match: structural correctness boundary in Temporal reducer/tool-state transition.
- `adv-codebase-design`: considered, not loaded; design-phase seam placement may use it later.

### Extends

- No `temp/*.md` prior notes found.
- `docs/repo-improve-prep.md`: relevant only as broad ADV tool performance context. New finding here: this change is not a performance/indexing issue; it is a typed state consistency issue in Epic terminal projection.
- `docs/non-coding-task-rigor-prep.md`: not directly relevant; confirms large non-code rigor, not this internal bugfix.
- Archived `fixEpicRepair`: relevant pattern — repair reporting must be honest and structural, not inferred from signal delivery. New finding: terminal projection has a similar honesty seam where display can report repair-needed after a terminal summary exists.
- Archived `addEpicRetirement`: relevant pattern — terminal history/read surfaces must remain typed and queryable after workflow completion. New finding: terminal history completeness also depends on `membership_status` consistency.
- Archived `fixRemoteEpicRouting`: relevant pattern — cross-project owner/child routing must remain explicit; terminal projection behavior is part of preserved same-project/cross-project membership semantics. New finding: retarget/sync paths can call terminal summary without terminal membership.
- Archived `addEpicTimestamps`: relevant only for Epic list/read surface discipline; confirms no need to add dashboard/indexing work here.

### Conflict Scan

- Active related work: `optimizeAdapterSurfaces` is adjacent but broader adapter-coupling work; keep this fix focused and separate.
- Active stale draft: `diagnoseArchivedListingTimeout`; no direct terminal-projection overlap found.
- Validation: `adv_change_validate strict:true` passed. Warnings `NO_TASKS` and `NO_DELTAS` expected before planning/spec deltas.
- Agenda: large agenda list returned; visible items were unrelated subagent follow-ups and target_path/archive/status work. No direct terminal-projection agenda item surfaced in the returned slice.

### Current State

- Spec law: `.adv/specs/advance-epics/spec.json:1140-1178` says a terminal child link must set `terminal_summary`, set `membership_status` to `terminal`, and later `adv_epic_show` must not show projection-missing/stale/repair-needed markers.
- Type support exists: `plugin/src/types/epics.ts:202-209` includes `terminal` in `EpicMembershipStatusSchema`.
- Presentation expects it: `plugin/src/tools/epic.ts:112-141` maps `linked` or `terminal` to `member_status.status: "ok"`; pending falls through to `projection_missing`.
- Reducer mismatch: `plugin/src/temporal/epic-state.ts:687-690` writes only `entry.terminal_summary`; it does not set `entry.membership_status`.
- Direct link path is correct: `plugin/src/tools/epic.ts:391-401` calls `setEntryTerminalSummary` and then `setEntryMembershipStatus(... "terminal")`.
- Retarget/sync/archive paths are suspect: `plugin/src/tools/epic.ts:2997-3001`, `plugin/src/tools/epic.ts:3193-3198`, and `plugin/src/tools/change/archive-gate.ts:516-520` call only `setEntryTerminalSummary`.
- Store surface returns the queried entry after terminal summary signal: `plugin/src/storage/store-temporal/epics.ts:882-915`, so if reducer does not set membership status, callers see the old status.
- Tests currently prove terminal summary/progress but not terminal membership in reducer/workflow: `plugin/src/temporal/epic-state.test.ts:611-660`, `plugin/src/temporal/workflows.epic.test.ts:298-317`.
- Some tool tests mock terminal membership, masking the underlying reducer issue: `plugin/src/tools/change.archive-phase9.test.ts:257-271`.

### Edge Cases

Gap: terminal summary projection can leave stale membership state.

1. Existing entry has `membership_status: "projection_pending"`; archive sync records `terminal_summary`; `memberStatusForEntry` returns `projection_missing` even though entry is terminal.
2. Existing entry has `membership_status: "target_unreachable"`; later terminal sync succeeds on owner workflow; display may keep target-unreachable status despite terminal history.
3. Shell entry receives terminal-summary signal by mistake; existing reducer correctly returns `entry_not_found` and must keep doing so.
4. Duplicate/idempotent terminal-summary signal should not regress idempotency or progress recomputation.
5. Direct link of already archived/closed child already sets terminal status; fix must not double-write or break that path.
6. Partial failure in any tool-level multi-call path must remain explicit; no display-only masking of real state failure.

### Open Design Questions

1. Where should terminal membership consistency be enforced?
   - Trust model: agent-owned technical decision.
   - Blast radius: reducer-level change affects every terminal-summary signal; tool-level change risks missing future call sites.

# Problem Statement

When an Epic-linked change is archived or terminal state is synchronized, ADV records a `terminal_summary` on the Epic entry but may leave `membership_status` as `projection_pending`, `projection_stale`, or `target_unreachable`. That can make terminal Epic history appear to need repair even though terminal projection exists.

Desired outcome: terminal child projection should be internally consistent and spec-aligned: Epic entries with terminal summaries should also reflect terminal membership status, with tests guarding the archive/sync path.

# Design

## Architecture Overview

Make `entryTerminalSummary` the structural state-transition boundary for Epic terminal projection consistency.

Today, terminal projection is split: some tool paths call `setEntryTerminalSummary` and then separately set `membership_status: "terminal"`, while other paths call only `setEntryTerminalSummary`. The reducer behind `entryTerminalSummary` records `terminal_summary` but leaves the existing `membership_status` untouched. That creates a typed-state seam where an entry can be terminal for progress/history but still look projection-missing/stale/unreachable for membership health.

Target architecture:

1. `applyEntryTerminalSummaryToState` sets both:
   - `entry.terminal_summary = { status, completed_at }`
   - `entry.membership_status = "terminal"`
2. All terminal-summary signal callers inherit consistent state through one Temporal reducer path.
3. Renderers continue using `membership_status` as source of truth for membership health; no display-only override is added.
4. Tool-level paths preserve explicit warnings/errors for failed signals or unreachable owner workflows.
5. Tests verify reducer/workflow state and at least one previously summary-only caller path.

## Key Decisions

### KD1 — Enforce terminal membership in the reducer

`applyEntryTerminalSummaryToState` is the single structural authority for terminal summary projection. When it succeeds for a change entry, it also normalizes `membership_status` to `terminal`.

Rationale:

- `setEntryTerminalSummary` is the common store API used by archive fan-out, repair sync, retarget, direct link, and workflow tests.
- `rq-epicTerminalChildProjection01` requires terminal summary and terminal membership to move together.
- A renderer fallback would hide inconsistent typed state and violate the agreement avoidance.
- Tool-level fixes would be easy to miss in future call sites.

### KD2 — Preserve explicit failure behavior

The operation is considered consistent only when the terminal-summary signal succeeds and queried state reflects terminal membership. If the signal fails, the existing tool/archive warning/failure path remains visible. No caller should claim repaired/OK solely by checking `terminal_summary` in presentation code.

### KD3 — Keep direct terminal link compatible, but allow redundant cleanup if tests prove safe

The direct archived/closed link path already calls `setEntryTerminalSummary` and `setEntryMembershipStatus("terminal")`. After reducer normalization, the second call is redundant. Implementation may either:

- leave the second call intact for minimal behavior churn; or
- remove/adjust it if focused RED/GREEN tests prove response shape and error behavior remain correct.

Either way, direct link behavior must still return terminal summary projected and `member_status.status: "ok"`.

### KD4 — Scope signal-name parity guard out unless touched naturally

Epic signal-name parity test is useful but not contract-critical for this fix. It may be added only if implementation naturally touches the signal surface and the test is local/cheap.

## ADR Drafts

None. Decisions are localized, reversible, and directly implied by existing spec law; no ADR needed.

## Implementation Strategy

1. Add RED coverage around reducer/workflow behavior:
   - `applyEntryTerminalSummaryToState` changes a `projection_pending` change entry to `membership_status: "terminal"`.
   - archived and closed terminal summaries both normalize membership.
   - shell/missing-entry/idempotency behavior remains unchanged.
2. Add targeted coverage for a previously summary-only caller:
   - preferred: archive fan-out or `sync_child_projection` repair path returns/renders terminal member status after summary projection;
   - acceptable: workflow integration test proves `entryTerminalSummarySignal` alone normalizes membership.
3. Update `applyEntryTerminalSummaryToState` to set `entry.membership_status = "terminal"` in the same mutation that writes `terminal_summary`.
4. Review direct link tests. Preserve or simplify the redundant explicit `setEntryMembershipStatus("terminal")` call only with regression proof.
5. Verify targeted suites covering Epic reducer/workflow/tool/archive path.

## LBP Analysis

Reducer-level normalization is the preferred long-term approach because it makes correctness structural in the state machine. Every caller of `setEntryTerminalSummary` gets the same invariant, including future callers. Tool-level duplicated calls would recreate the current inconsistency risk, and renderer-only fixes would mask drift instead of correcting state.

## Affected Components

- `plugin/src/temporal/epic-state.ts` — terminal summary reducer normalization.
- `plugin/src/temporal/epic-state.test.ts` — reducer regression coverage.
- `plugin/src/temporal/workflows.epic.test.ts` or related workflow tests — signal-level coverage.
- `plugin/src/tools/epic.ts` — direct link / repair / retarget behavior review; possible test adjustments only.
- `plugin/src/tools/change/archive-gate.ts` and `plugin/src/tools/change.archive-phase9.test.ts` — archive fan-out coverage if chosen as the caller-path regression.
- `plugin/src/storage/store-temporal/epics.ts` — no design change expected; returns queried entry after signal.

## Design-Derived Criteria

- DDC1: The invariant `terminal_summary != null` for a change entry implies `membership_status === "terminal"` after any successful `entryTerminalSummary` reducer application.
- DDC2: No renderer may treat stale membership as OK solely because `terminal_summary` exists.
- DDC3: Tests must include a starting membership state other than `terminal` (for example `projection_pending` or `target_unreachable`) before terminal projection.
- DDC4: Idempotent replay of the same terminal-summary signal must not regress terminal membership or progress.

## Risks / Mitigations

- Risk: reducer-level change affects all terminal-summary callers.
  - Mitigation: this is intended; add workflow/reducer tests and preserve existing shell/missing-entry errors.
- Risk: direct link path may perform redundant terminal status signal.
  - Mitigation: keep for compatibility unless local tests prove safe simplification.
- Risk: archive test mocks can still mask real state behavior.
  - Mitigation: add at least one real reducer/workflow assertion that starts from non-terminal membership.
- Risk: partial failure semantics could change if multiple tool calls are removed.
  - Mitigation: preserve explicit failure/warning behavior and avoid display-only success.

## Design Leverage Scout

Scout: skipped — focused state-machine bugfix with existing spec law, known reducer seam, and no user-value tradeoff or broad opportunity surface.

## Validator Result

Validator: clean pass ✓

- `validation.status: pass`, confidence high, risk low.
- Finding: reducer normalization is correct and spec-implied.
- Source evidence: `.adv/specs/advance-epics/spec.json:1142-1178`, `plugin/src/temporal/epic-state.ts:687-690`, `plugin/src/tools/epic.ts:112-141,391-402`, `plugin/src/tools/change/archive-gate.ts:516-529`.
- Alternatives considered and rejected: tool-level fixes are non-structural across 3+ call sites; renderer-only fix masks drift and violates the agreement avoidance.
- Planning notes: write `membership_status = "terminal"` in the same reducer mutation block before idempotency record; RED tests must start from non-terminal membership state.
